samples.reverse_paraphrase: The source editor says this chapter still needs review, expansion and exercises; the Gujarati editorial retains the limitation.
Partial computability allows undefined arguments, whereas computable without qualification is total; weak equality also agrees when both sides are undefined.
Every computation model allows finite descriptions, syntactic recognition, numerical coding and effective simulation of coded programs.
A unary partial computable function is represented by primitive-recursive T and U with one unbounded search; higher arities require coding.
The primitive recursive s^m_n specializes the first m arguments of an m+n-ary indexed program and yields an n-ary index.
The illustrative program input is e in both the specialization formula and its Turing-machine reading; the frozen x is disclosed as an error.
One binary partial function evaluates every indexed unary partial computable function; universality permits undefined cases.
If a total computable universal listing existed, adding one to its diagonal value would yield a total computable function absent from the list.
A halting decider would turn the partial universal evaluator into a total computable universal evaluator, contradicting the preceding theorem.
The second proof makes a program defined on x exactly when the supposed halting answer says its self-application is undefined.
Russell's set belongs to itself exactly when it does not; the source's capital X is not the set under discussion.
The diagonal 0/1 function is a legitimate set-theoretic function but not one of the computable functions it diagonalizes against.
Membership in S is computable exactly when its characteristic function returns 1 for members and 0 otherwise.
A c.e. set is empty or the range of a total computable function; the separate empty case matters.
A c.e. set can equivalently be a nonempty computable range, a partial-computable range, a primitive-recursive range, or a partial-computable domain, with empty exceptions as stated.
A pair-code z witnessing the primitive-recursive enumerator uses its first component as the input of phi_e, not an unbound x.
The empty c.e. set is a partial-computable domain via a nowhere-defined function; no total computable function can have empty range.
Existential projection of a computable relation is c.e., and an unbounded search yields a partial function with precisely that domain.
The domain search for K_0 halts exactly for program-input pairs with a halting computation code.
Searching the two computable enumerations in parallel semi-decides union; finding both witnesses semi-decides intersection.
The first halting witness among the A and complement programs decides membership; d, not e, identifies A.
The informal two-machine explanation must use the same d and e indices as the proof, and d's success means x lies in A.
The halting-pair set codes index e before input x; mapping x to its diagonal pair reduces self-halting to pair-halting.
A many-one reduction is total computable and preserves yes and no answers to set membership.
If B is c.e. and A reduces to B, composing A's reduction with B's partial domain witness makes A c.e.
To establish completeness of K, the proof needs the hard pair-halting set K_0 to reduce to K; the frozen sentence states the reverse.
An index for a program ignoring its input can encode whether phi_e(x) halts; testing it at zero decides the original pair-halting question.
The constructed program indexed by k(x) is total if x self-halts and nowhere defined otherwise, reducing K to Tot.
Rice's theorem permits decidable syntax checks while ruling out nontrivial semantic questions about the computed function.
The h used before s-m-n has two arguments and therefore requires a binary-function index; the Gujarati arity is explicit.
The diagonal map turns a binary program index into a unary program index by fixing the original index as its first argument.
The indexed l in the fixed-point calculation is binary, so its own index is supplied as the first input while y remains the second.
The selector under refutation may be partial; if its value is undefined at the computable fixed-point domain, the promised definedness already fails.
The fixed-point theorem supplies a function that either returns k(y) or recurses through m(y), with partiality allowed.
The gcd recursion applies Euclid's remainder step until the first argument is zero, and descent proves totality.
